stem: A pregnant client at 34 weeks develops sudden vaginal bleeding without abdominal or back pain and without contractions. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?

options.B: Preterm labor with bloody cervical discharge
options.C: Bleeding from cervical inflammation or a cervical growth

rationale: ACOG states that placenta previa may cause vaginal bleeding later in pregnancy and that this bleeding often occurs without pain. In contrast, placental abruption commonly presents with vaginal bleeding plus abdominal or back pain, while preterm labor generally includes contractions or other labor-related changes and cervical causes more commonly produce light bleeding. Therefore, painless third-trimester bleeding without contractions is most consistent with placenta previa, although any bleeding late in pregnancy requires prompt obstetric evaluation.
educational_objective: Recognize painless vaginal bleeding later in pregnancy as a presentation that is particularly consistent with placenta previa and requires prompt obstetric evaluation.
source_organization: American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG)
source_version_date: Last updated May 2021; last reviewed December 2024
source_locator: FAQ → 'What problems can cause bleeding later in pregnancy?'; 'What problems with the placenta can cause bleeding during pregnancy?' sections for placental abruption and placenta previa; preterm-labor section.
source_claim_supported: ACOG states that placenta previa bleeding often occurs without pain; placental abruption commonly includes abdominal or back pain; preterm labor may include bloody discharge and contractions; any late-pregnancy bleeding warrants prompt evaluation.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation → Alterations in Body Systems/Medical Emergencies and complications of pregnancy requiring recognition and prompt intervention.

source_original.stem: A pregnant client at 34 weeks with intact membranes develops sudden painless bright-red vaginal bleeding. The fetal heart tracing is reassuring. Which condition is most consistent with this presentation?
source_original.rationale: ACOG describes placenta previa as a cause of later-pregnancy vaginal bleeding that often occurs without pain. Placental abruption more often includes abdominal or back pain. Intact membranes and a reassuring fetal tracing make vasa previa less consistent with the complete presentation, though any third-trimester bleeding requires urgent obstetric evaluation.
source_original.source_detail: ACOG Bleeding During Pregnancy — placental causes later in pregnancy: placental abruption commonly includes abdominal/back pain; placenta previa bleeding often occurs without pain. ACOG page last reviewed 2024-12; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Physiological Adaptation; acute/complex alterations and medical emergencies. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Rewrote the stem and distractors to eliminate unsupported precision and avoid using intact membranes/reassuring fetal tracing as an unsourced rule-out for vasa previa. Removed the 'bright-red' descriptor because the cited ACOG page supports painless bleeding but not that exact color descriptor. The final item is fully anchored to ACOG's late-pregnancy bleeding distinctions. Difficulty recalibrated from hard to medium.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Third-trimester vaginal bleeding — placenta previa versus other causes
audit_findings.currentness: ACOG page last reviewed December 2024 and rechecked 2026-08-16.
audit_findings.exact_locator: Placenta previa and placental abruption sections directly support pain distinction; late-pregnancy bleeding/preterm-labor sections support comparators.
audit_findings.claim_audit: Removed bright-red specificity and vasa-previa inference because the cited source did not directly support those precision claims.

distractor_audit.A: Plausible placental cause but less consistent because ACOG commonly associates abruption with abdominal/back pain.
distractor_audit.B: Plausible late-pregnancy bleeding cause but absence of contractions/labor changes makes it less consistent.
distractor_audit.C: Cervical causes can bleed but ACOG describes them among lighter later-pregnancy bleeding causes rather than the classic painless placental presentation.
distractor_audit.D: Uniquely best because ACOG specifically notes placenta previa bleeding often occurs without pain.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: The revised stem emphasizes the discriminating pain/contraction pattern and removes vasa previa, leaving D as the best supported answer.
audit_findings.cueing: All options are recognized causes of later-pregnancy bleeding.
audit_findings.blueprint: Direct Physiological Adaptation relevance through recognition of a potentially serious placental complication.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Adversarial review identified and removed the prior unsupported vasa-previa exclusion and bright-red precision.
